context: Request: the firm's deals over $1B in guaranteed (base) consideration, excluding earnout/CVR value, governed by Delaware law. divergence: Mixed (T0, T2 pass; T1 fails). All three runs had their first store-wide extraction scan time out. They split right there: T0 reran the scan as background range jobs and T2 as parallel shards with saved output, so both got complete value and governing-law hits, screened the billion-scale candidates and verified their executed agreements (T0 added an unfiltered rescan after its review flagged a file-name filter). T1 instead read agreements picked from its file inventory, then ran a value scan limited to agreement-like file names whose unfiltered rerun timed out; two needed deals never surfaced, and a third was dropped after a guessed path failed. T1's reviews named both the file-name filter and the failed path; the agent wrote one deal anyway. Reviews did not differ in kind between the runs; the passing runs acted on the scan-coverage flags. Agent-declared new stages (background scan, targeted extraction, completeness checks) mapped to scan, snippet and in-depth stages.
